problem: Existing test-time adaptation for VLN needs access to the training (source) data and all test data before inference, which is impractical when an agent is deployed in a new environment. Naive online adaptation with a single test sample causes catastrophic forgetting and unstable parameter updates.
motivation: Models trained on seen environments degrade on unseen environments because of distribution shift. A practical deployment setting must be source-free and online, where the model sees only one test sample at a time. This requires an adaptation scheme that is stable and does not destroy learned knowledge.
key_idea: Adapt a small auxiliary decision model online on incoming test samples, with a sample replay buffer for stability, while the original model stays frozen and the two jointly make action decisions.
insight: Keeping the original model frozen and updating only an auxiliary model limits catastrophic forgetting, while replaying stored historical test samples stabilizes the online updates. The abstract reports gains on three base methods across three VLN benchmarks, which supports model-agnostic use. No ablation details are available because only the abstract was provided.
method: Auxiliary decision model: a model adapted online with test samples to the new environment
Frozen original model: keeps the source knowledge and cooperates with the auxiliary model to choose actions
Sample replay mechanism: stores historical test samples and replays them to make adaptation more stable
Source-free online setting: only one test sample is accessible for adaptation at a time, with no training data access
Model-agnostic plug-in: applicable to most existing VLN methods

setting.backbone: three existing VLN methods (unspecified in abstract), frozen, plus an auxiliary decision model adapted online
setting.training_data: Base models trained as originally; the adaptation uses only online test samples with no source data

results: The abstract states that the method achieves stable performance improvement over three existing VLN methods on three VLN benchmark datasets. No specific numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details and numbers are unknown
